Daily Devotional

March 1

4 Behold, his soul which is lifted up is not upright in him: but the just shall live by his faith. (Habakkuk 2:4 KJV)

This verse is telling us that pride is an ungodly attitude and is contrasted with faith (Proverbs16:18; Matthew 5:5, 11:29; James 4:6; and 1 Peter 5:5). So we can see that part of faith is being humble and dependent on God rather than ourselves.

The end of this verse is quoted three times in the New Testament (Romans 1:17, Galatians 3:11, and Hebrews 10:38). In each instance in the New Testament, this verse was cited to show that salvation is by grace through faith (Ephesians 2:8), instead of our own works or effort. Even though most Christian religions tend to teach a combination of salvation by grace and works, the true Gospel of Jesus Christ is that we are saved entirely by grace through faith. That way God gets all the credit for our salvation, and we don’t get any for our works of the law. It seems that most churches still want to preach that we are saved by grace through the sacrifice that Jesus made. But then we have to do a bunch of works of the law (like attend church, tithe, live holy, etc.) or God will not bless us or answer our prayers. And that is just not so. That is mixing grace and works of the law, and is not what the bible teaches (Romans 11:6). The “Good News” of the Gospel, is that we are saved by Grace, without the works of the law – Thank you Jesus!

Devotional by Pastor Joe W. Green, www.Infinite-Faith.com
